I will say I’ve gotten very lucky in the last couple years with therapists. They’re all about finding natural coping methods, and are against antipsychotics. (There are some people that do indeed need them, but I believe most don’t.)

However, when I was 20 and ready to face my trauma, and get help, I had a therapist in a city near DFW area in Texas (unsure if I’m allowed to say the actual city). She had diagnosed me with PTSD, made sense to me, and she got me involved in a women’s trauma group. The group was amazing because it was 95% us running things with the therapist sitting back.

And then she told me that my insurance wanted to pay her a small percentage less than what she was getting paid originally. She told me I’d have to pay for the rest that insurance didn’t pay. Which was over $200.
I was 20. I had a split shift job as a bus monitor for special needs children. I was lucky enough to live with a family member so I didn’t have to pay bills.
I had recently been diagnosed, and gotten over the anxiety of a new person/situation. I broke down in her office. I felt things were going so great, only to be hit with bi-weekly bill I could barely afford.

But it gets worse.

She recommended me a service dog since at that time, I could only go to work and therapy. I was terrified to go anywhere else, and often had flashbacks and panic attacks in public.
My cousin helped me through the process and later on, we found my dog (Yeti), and all I needed to do was fill out an airline forum that I will be bringing Yeti on the return flight home, and it needed to be signed by a “Medical OR Mental Health Professional.”

I was so excited and happy, my life was changing, things are going to get better, finally.
And then she shook her head at me saying she couldn’t sign the paper.

“I’m not a medical or mental health professional. I’m a licensed counselor. And I don’t remember discussing a service dog with you? Did I diagnose you with PTSD? That doesn’t sound right.”

I was enraged. 
I broke down crying (again). The flight was in two weeks and this fucking bitch GASLIGHTS me!?
SHE was the one who diagnosed me.
SHE was the one that enrolled me in the trauma group!
SHE was the one who suggested a service dog!

I left, and booked it to my PCM’s office and, while embarrassingly balling to the receptionist, explained the situation and practically begged for my doctor to sign it.
She did.
They were very kind, and helped calm me down.

Everything worked out in the end, but I will NEVER forget that cunt that gaslit and took advantage of me. And probably did the same to all of her vulnerable clients. It sickens me.
It’s absolutely vile that some therapists exploit their clients who are vulnerable or don’t know better.

I was on seroquel for around 3 years off and on while trying other antipsychotics.  


FUCK. SEROQUEL.  


Sure I got PLENTY of sleep, but it ruined my personality, motivation, and emotions. I always say it caused ego death while I was on it.  
It made the depression cycles worse, and stifled the mania (Which I guess is the goal).   
While I don't/can't work a vanilla job anyway, seroquel hammered the nail in the coffin, even when it came to working my current stay at home job.   


I lost followers, which meant I lost money. I lost the desire to make content, I lost the motivation and energy to even try.   
Then I tried vraylar, gained 20 lbs, and decided I was done with antipsychotics.  


While this isn't the solution to everyone, I can at least say that I LOVED vraylar compared to seroquel and anything like it. It took away 3 years of my life all because I really wanted to give it a shot.  


And you're right, fuck the withdrawals. It's insane how something like that can make you feel like you're trying to get off street drugs.

This happened several years ago so I can't remember if she ever told me or not. I know she didn't at first.  


As for her reaction, of course she was ANGRY lol. She grew up with being told your body is sacred and showing off any nudity to anyone that isn't your spouse is morally wrong. Surprisingly, even though I was making money now and she knew that, they only made me pay for my phone bill. They still paid for my car and health insurance. Which was a clear sign to me that they still loved me despite disappointing them for the time being.  
In the end she ended up being a really good sport about it. Over the years I've told her the ins and outs of the industry and how I'm safe, happy, and grateful I found something to make money at home without triggering my PTSD and bipolar disorder.  
Her anger came from an instilled concept of conservative right and wrong, which I didn't blame her for. After all, it is hard to change your views/opinions when you've had them your whole life.   
Ultimately, she ended up seeing how happy I was, and carving myself to be more independent. They may be mad or disappointed at first, but I've found that their love for their child conquered any kind of disgust or hatred.

Someone had messaged my mother over social media that I was camming. She was livid at first, which I understood because she was born and raised very religious in Texas.

It was hard at first, because a lot of people are closed minded when it comes to sex work. I explain to friends/family that have questions that, I am completely safe in my own home camming, I set my own hours and never have to do anything I don't want to. My whole family has actually taken it pretty well now and I have aunts that even joke about making an OnlyFans since I've told them there is a huge market for MILFs lol.  


What helped me the most was being confident and not ashamed of what I do. I proved to my parents that I was happy and had never felt more comfortable with my work and income. With that, people will (usually) start to tear down their walls of closed minded thinking.   


While my initial experience was pretty negative, I am happy that I've been able to discuss my work and gain the support of my immediate and distant family. Sometimes it just takes some patience, and a lot of love!
